title: Reversibly restore youthful function across an aged organism

concept.text: The proposed innovation is to restore multiple functions that have declined with age across an already aged organism, sustain those improvements, and preserve the specialized identities and coordinated activity of its cells and tissues. Success would require improvements in how the organism functions and withstands stress, rather than changes in molecular markers alone. Here, reversibility refers to reversing age-associated functional deficits; it does not establish that treatment effects could be freely switched on and off.

Partial cellular reprogramming is one documented route toward this goal. It attempts to recover youthful characteristics through changes in cell state while avoiding full dedifferentiation, in which specialized cells lose their identities. The broader innovation is not restricted to reprogramming, and it does not assume that aging has a single root cause. Improvements in individual cells or tissues would need to translate into durable benefits across interacting aged systems.

significance.text: If achieved reliably, broad rejuvenation would establish that multiple age-associated functional deficits can be experimentally reversed in the demonstrated organism. That would extend the significance of reported tissue-specific functional improvements: the advance would be coordinated restoration across aged systems, with benefits that persist beyond an immediate treatment response.

Conditional synthesis: Such a capability could provide a basis for interventions that address several consequences of aging together and could help researchers test which age-associated changes actually drive functional decline. These possibilities depend on identifying what the intervention changes, demonstrating useful functional effects, and establishing that benefits outweigh harm. They are prospective consequences of the proposed breakthrough.

The demonstrated organism and treatment conditions would bound the initial impact. Restoration in mice would not establish comparable effects in humans, prevention or elimination of particular diseases, or the safety of repeated treatment. Centuries-long human lifespan and elimination of age-related disease are unsupported extrapolations from the supplied evidence. A younger molecular age estimate is also not equivalent to a rejuvenated organism.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is dependable, sustained restoration across multiple aged systems while retaining normal cellular identity and acceptable long-term safety. Partial reprogramming exposes a central biological difficulty: factors used to change cell state can activate programs associated with pluripotency and proliferation while suppressing specialized cell identity. The desired restoration must therefore be separated from uncontrolled growth, teratoma formation, and loss of tissue function.

Delivery and tissue-specific responses are additional barriers. An organism-wide intervention must reach relevant cells and produce appropriate effects across tissues that may respond differently. Benefit in one tissue cannot establish safety or efficacy in another. The perspective consequently identifies investigation of each tissue and system as necessary for therapeutic translation; broad restoration cannot be inferred from a favorable result at a single site.

Persistence and measurement remain unresolved. Improvements must last long enough to distinguish durable restoration from a transient response, and their assessment must connect molecular changes to function, resilience, and survival. Epigenetic clock reversal may suggest rejuvenation, but the perspective explicitly distinguishes the two. A convincing intervention must also establish whether benefits persist after treatment and whether any repeated dosing introduces cumulative harm.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence centers on Yücel and Gladyshev’s 2024 perspective, “The long and winding road of reprogramming-induced rejuvenation,” DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-46020-5. Its publication date is supplied as March 2, 2024; the validated review verified the document’s identity and year but did not independently establish the exact publication day from its text. The perspective reviews progress and limitations in partial reprogramming rather than reporting completion of broad organismal rejuvenation.

According to the supplied review, the perspective reports encouraging mouse molecular, functional, and survival findings and discusses restoration of visual function as a tissue-specific application. These findings provide a basis for investigating rejuvenation, but their scope does not establish dependable restoration across an aged organism. Molecular changes, recovery of a particular function, and survival effects are distinct outcomes; one should not be substituted for another.

The perspective’s reported remaining-lifespan finding cites a 2023 bioRxiv preprint. That result must therefore retain its preprint qualification in this record. The underlying primary studies were not supplied for independent assessment, and the supplied review does not provide a numerical effect size suitable for preservation here. This limits the conclusions that can be drawn about magnitude and robustness; it does not show that the reported result is false.

The perspective leaves substantial questions about safety, delivery, measurement, tissue-specific responses, and the longevity of rejuvenation effects unresolved. The supplied review had complete extracted text spanning the document, with minor spacing issues that did not prevent its textual judgments. Its conclusions did not require figure inspection. Access to that review of the literature does not amount to independent verification of every experiment it cites.

Evidence boundary: This is a dated assessment of the supplied 2024 perspective. The supplied freshness search record is empty, so it does not establish the field’s status on November 1, 2026, or at the later source-retrieval date of November 11, 2026. Retrieval of an older document does not update its scientific coverage. The supported conclusion is that the reviewed findings do not establish the proposed breakthrough; whether later work changes that assessment remains unestablished in these inputs.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Conduct independently replicated studies in naturally aged mammals showing sustained restoration of multiple organ functions and resilience, together with improved survival. Include age-matched controls to estimate treatment effects and younger animals to characterize the extent of functional restoration. Naturally aged subjects would directly test the intended aging context, while independent replication would test whether the result survives differences between research settings. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Replicated aged-mammal studies show lasting multiorgan, resilience, and survival gains

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement and safety requirements: Combine functional outcomes with molecular measurements, and monitor for cancer, abnormal growth, and loss of specialized cell identity over an appropriately long follow-up. Molecular age clocks alone would not establish completion. Assess persistence after treatment and, if repeated treatment is proposed, evaluate the benefits and harms of that schedule. These requirements respond to the perspective’s documented measurement, safety, and persistence concerns; their precise implementation would need a defined experimental protocol.
completion_criteria.label: Report functional and molecular outcomes, long-term safety, and treatment persistence

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: Specify the organs and functions tested, starting ages and health conditions, intervention and delivery method, effect sizes, follow-up duration, and acceptable safety thresholds before interpreting success. Report failures and uneven responses alongside improvements. Finite experiments would establish the breadth and durability demonstrated under those conditions, not literal universality across tissues, species, or individuals. Human benefit and safe repeated use would require their own evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Report prespecified experimental boundaries, safety thresholds, and uneven treatment outcomes

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIO-06, “Enable complete, patterned regeneration of complex mammalian structures,” shares the need to restore function while controlling cell identity, growth, and tissue organization. Its defining target is reconstruction of a complex structure; BIO-07 targets restoration across aged systems. Either capability could aid the other, but regeneration of one structure would not establish broad rejuvenation, and rejuvenation would not establish complete patterned regeneration.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-15, “Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body,” overlaps with the challenge of reaching appropriate cells throughout an organism. Selective delivery could enable some rejuvenation strategies, but genome editing is not required by BIO-07’s definition. Successful delivery alone would not establish restoration of youthful function, while a successful rejuvenation intervention would not necessarily demonstrate broadly programmable genome editing.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-10, “Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale,” could support measurements of treatment response and preservation of cell identity. BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins,” could help distinguish causal drivers of aging-related decline from correlated molecular changes. Both could strengthen the mechanistic basis of rejuvenation, but molecular observation or causal annotation alone would not demonstrate organismal functional restoration.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-03, “Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts,” and BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” could help anticipate context-dependent benefits and harms of candidate interventions. Their targets are predictive capabilities. BIO-07 requires experimental restoration in aged organisms, including interactions across tissues and long-term outcomes that cannot be established solely by accurate predictions in selected cellular settings.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-09, “Observe and causally test whole-brain computation at cellular resolution,” and BIO-13, “Establish the physical mechanisms that store and retrieve a long-term memory,” would become relevant when evaluating claims about rejuvenation of neural function. They concern brain computation and memory mechanisms, respectively. Restoring selected age-associated neural functions would not by itself resolve either target, and progress on either target would not establish broad rejuvenation.

change_log.change: Preserved BIO-07’s identity and organism-wide functional target while clarifying the meaning of reversal.
change_log.reason: The concept concerns reversal of age-associated deficits; the supplied evidence does not establish freely switchable treatment effects.

change_log.change: Integrated partial reprogramming as a documented route without making it the sole mechanism or assuming one root cause of aging.
change_log.reason: The review supports reprogramming’s relevance while preserving the broader biological scope of the innovation.

change_log.change: Expanded the barriers to include cell identity, uncontrolled growth, tissue-specific responses, delivery, persistence, and measurement.
change_log.reason: These distinctions explain why encouraging cellular and tissue findings do not establish dependable restoration across an organism.

change_log.change: Separated molecular, functional, and survival findings and retained the preprint qualification for the remaining-lifespan result.
change_log.reason: Different endpoints support different conclusions, and the cited lifespan source was identified as a 2023 bioRxiv preprint.

change_log.change: Qualified the exact publication date and limited the current-state assessment to the supplied dated evidence.
change_log.reason: The review verified the source’s identity and year, while the exact day came from metadata and the freshness search record was empty.

change_log.change: Preserved the primary-study and extraction boundaries without treating them as evidence against reported results.
change_log.reason: The review used complete extracted perspective text, but primary experiments were not independently assessed.

change_log.change: Developed completion criteria into explicit proposals for replication, functional breadth, survival, safety, and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: The review supports their rationale but identifies no established protocol, numerical thresholds, or consensus standard.

unresolved_issues: The supplied inputs do not establish whether developments after the 2024 perspective change the assessment, including as of November 1, 2026.
The exact March 2, 2024 publication date remains supplied metadata rather than a date independently established from the document text by the review.

Primary studies underlying the reported mouse outcomes were not supplied for independent assessment; their detailed protocols, numerical effects, reproducibility, and subsequent publication history remain unassessed here.
A completion protocol still needs defined organ coverage, effect sizes, resilience measures, follow-up duration, and acceptable safety thresholds.
The persistence of benefits, safety of repeated treatment, and translation to humans remain unresolved.
No historical comparison examples were supplied, so no claim of demonstrated equivalence to an earlier scientific revolution is made.

brief.title: Restoring youthful function throughout an aged body
possible: An aged body could regain abilities lost with age across several organs, with lasting improvements in function and the ability to withstand stress. Its cells would keep doing their specialized jobs.
why: This could provide a basis for treatments that address several consequences of ageing together. Researchers could also use it to test which changes associated with ageing actually cause the body to lose function.

sources.who: Ali Doğa Yücel and Vadim N. Gladyshev
sources.showed: They reviewed partial reprogramming, which shifts cells towards a younger state while aiming to preserve their specialized roles. They described reports of restored vision and improved tissue repair in mice.
sources.quote:
Moreover, this treatment increased skin regeneration
capacity in mice15.
sources.cited_for: The review describes functional improvements in individual tissues and the barriers to restoring function throughout the body.
sources.not_established: Tissue improvements do not establish lasting restoration across an aged body.

sources.who: Anissa A. Widjaja, Stuart A. Cook and collaborators
sources.showed: Blocking IL-11, a signal that promotes inflammation, improved metabolism and muscle function, reduced frailty and extended lifespan in aged mice of both sexes.
sources.quote:
In lifespan studies, genetic deletion of Il11 extended the lives 
of mice of both sexes, by 24.9% on average.
sources.cited_for: A treatment begun in aged mice improved several measures of health alongside survival.
sources.not_established: The findings do not establish independently replicated, lasting restoration across organs or benefits after treatment stops.

sources.who: Carolina Cano Macip and colleagues at Rejuvenate Bio and Whitehead Institute
sources.showed: This group delivered genes for partial reprogramming to very old male mice. Median remaining lifespan increased by 109%, and frailty improved.
sources.quote: Importantly, we observed a significant improvement in frailty scores indicating that we were able to improve the healthspan along with increasing the lifespan.
sources.cited_for: Partial reprogramming improved survival and measured health in naturally aged mice.
sources.not_established: A result in male mice from one group does not establish reproducibility, broad organ restoration or long-term safety.

sources.who: Mirco J. Friedrich, Feng Zhang and collaborators
sources.showed: They made the liver temporarily produce signals that support immune cells. Aged mice responded better to vaccines and fought tumours more effectively.
sources.quote:
These effects were reversible after dosing ceased and did not breach 
self-tolerance
sources.cited_for: Immune function can improve in aged mice, but those gains can depend on continued treatment.
sources.not_established: The immune benefits faded after treatment stopped, and the work did not demonstrate restoration across aged organs.

sources.who: Alejandro Ocampo, Juan Carlos Izpisua Belmonte and collaborators
sources.showed: Partial reprogramming extended lifespan in mice with premature ageing and improved recovery from pancreatic and muscle injury in older mice without that condition.
sources.quote: Similarly, expression of OSKM in vivo improves recovery from metabolic disease and muscle injury in older wild-type mice.
sources.cited_for: Early experiments linked partial reprogramming to tissue recovery and survival benefits.
sources.not_established: Survival gains in premature ageing and injury recovery do not establish broad restoration in naturally aged animals.

shown: Researchers have improved several aspects of health alongside survival in aged mice. Widjaja, Cook and colleagues did so by blocking an inflammation signal. Cano Macip and colleagues reported gains through partial reprogramming. Friedrich, Zhang and colleagues restored immune responses.
missing: Independent studies have yet to demonstrate lasting gains across multiple aged organs, resistance to stress and survival together.
Broad restoration has yet to preserve cells’ specialized roles while avoiding cancer, abnormal growth and loss of tissue function over the long term.
Treatment has yet to reach the relevant tissues reliably and produce appropriate benefits despite their different responses.

milestones.label: Replicated, lasting gains across organs, stress resistance and survival
milestones.explanation: Independent studies in naturally aged mammals would have to show lasting gains against age-matched controls, with younger animals as benchmarks. This would test whether broad restoration holds across research settings.

milestones.label: Function, molecular changes, lasting effects and safety measured together
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to connect molecular changes to function, track cancer and cell identity, and assess benefits after stopping or repeating treatment. This would distinguish durable restoration from misleading signs of youth.

milestones.label: Success judged within predefined limits, including failures
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to define organs, starting health, treatment, effect sizes, follow-up and safety thresholds in advance, then report uneven results. This would establish where the treatment works and where it fails.

uncertain: The organ coverage, size of improvement, stress tests and follow-up needed to count as broad restoration remain undefined.
Whether benefits can persist after treatment, or repeated treatment can sustain them without accumulating harm, remains unresolved.
Whether comparable restoration could be achieved safely in humans remains unknown.

page.title: Multisystem functional rejuvenation
page.definition: A therapeutic intervention restores functions lost with age across several physiological systems in an already aged organism. A published human target combines recovery of muscle, cognitive and immune function in the same individuals.

goal.need: WHO’s 2024 estimates for 2021 show a 9.5-year difference between global life expectancy and healthy life expectancy at birth, calculated from their point estimates. This measures health loss across all causes. Recovering age-lost function addresses one component of that loss.

figures.caption: Global life expectancy at birth, both sexes, 2021

statements.quote: the competition challenges teams to restore muscle, cognitive, and immune function by at least 10 years

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
statements.quote: PROSPR aims to dramatically change this accepted trajectory by providing Americans with therapeutics that target the biology of aging directly.
statements.context: The preceding passage describes chronic conditions and functional limitations in older Americans.

completion.title: A therapy meets XPRIZE Healthspan’s 10-year restoration threshold across all three functional domains.
completion.criterion: In a randomized controlled trial of adults aged 50–90 years without major life-threatening disease or disability, treatment lasting ≤1 year produces ≥10-year-equivalent restoration in muscle, cognition and immunity within the same responders, using XPRIZE’s age-, sex- and baseline-specific thresholds. The responder proportion exceeds controls by ≥20 percentage points; the one-sided 90% confidence lower bound on that difference is ≥15 points. Judges also consider safety.
completion.set_by: XPRIZE Foundation, Competition Guidelines v2.2 and Finals Rules and Regulations v1.0, dated 13 April 2026.
completion.threshold_quote: a functional improvement of at least 10 years in all three systems (muscle, cognition, and immune), compared with controls
completion.basis: This is a published human multisystem target, narrower than whole-organism rejuvenation. Prize receipt alone is insufficient because the rules permit discretionary awards below threshold. Cell-identity preservation and persistence after withdrawal remain additional questions. The public rules defer the personalised threshold equations.

milestones.title: A treatment improves health and function in at least two aged tissues or organ systems.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate treatment-induced improvement in at least two tissues or organ systems. Ocampo et al. reported improved glucose tolerance after pancreatic injury in 12-month-old mice (6 treated, 6 controls) and improved muscle regeneration after injury (4 per group). Anti-IL-11 treatment from 75 to 100 weeks improved glucose tolerance and grip strength in male mice (12 treated, 13 antibody controls). These were separate studies and cohorts.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H, PROSPR solicitation ARPA-H-SOL-25-125, Appendix C, preliminary evidence for second-generation interventions.
milestones.threshold_quote: Provide evidence of improved health and function in response to therapeutic intervention in at least two tissues or organ systems.

milestones.title: A therapy preserves or improves five health metrics in aging rodents with independent validation.
milestones.criterion: In naturally aging outbred rodents of both sexes, treatment maintains or improves ≥5 health metrics (p<0.05), assessed at ≥2 post-treatment timepoints, with efficacy in ≥90%, no significant major-organ toxicity, ≥80% power, young/vehicle controls and independent-site validation. Intrinsic-capacity measures must track human measures (R²≥0.7), be repeatable and reproducible in ≥90% of animals, and show age decline and sex differences. A 2024 partial-reprogramming study in 124-week-old males (20 treated, 20 controls) increased median remaining lifespan by 109%; it did not test this composite endpoint.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H, PROSPR solicitation, Technical Area 3 Phase I and Table 5. The numerical efficacy criteria appear in the table; intrinsic capacity combines physical and mental abilities.

milestones.title: A rejuvenation drug reaches human dosing under an effective IND and ethics approval.
milestones.criterion: For a US investigational drug or biologic requiring an Investigational New Drug application, administer the intervention to human participants after institutional review board approval and IND effectiveness. An IND ordinarily becomes effective 30 days after FDA receipt if no clinical hold is imposed, or upon earlier FDA notification that testing may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, questions 5, 8 and 9; applies to the US drug and biologic development route.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A rejuvenation intervention completes human proof-of-concept testing and qualifies for XPRIZE Finals.
milestones.criterion: Complete human proof-of-concept testing that demonstrates feasibility and readiness for a larger clinical study, and obtain acceptance for Finals testing. Teams define study-specific go/no-go criteria; no common efficacy effect size is required at this stage. XPRIZE announced 20 finalist teams on 11 August 2026. This selection announcement is not peer-reviewed efficacy evidence.
milestones.set_by: XPRIZE Foundation, Qualifying Submissions Criteria and Judging, Part 2, and Competition Guidelines, Semi-Finals Testing.
milestones.threshold_quote: However, to advance through Semi-Finals (and Finals) clinical trials per defined criteria in the Competition Guidelines are required.

milestones.title: A rejuvenation intervention completes controlled human testing with at least 40 participants per arm.
milestones.criterion: Complete randomized controlled testing in adults aged 50–90 years, with at least 40 participants per arm. Obtain the specified muscle, cognitive, immune and safety assessments, including two baseline visits and follow-up visits at months 11 and 12 after randomization.
milestones.set_by: XPRIZE Foundation, Finals Rules and Regulations v1.0, sample-size provisions, and Healthspan Finals FAQ Issue 3, assessment schedule.
milestones.threshold_quote: Teams may enroll a minimum of 80 (40 per group)

not_found: No public update supplying XPRIZE’s personalised threshold equations or final immune-challenge assay was located.
No regulator or consensus test was located that combines whole-organism functional restoration, preserved cell identity and benefit after withdrawal.
No independent study satisfying the complete PROSPR preclinical validation criteria or completed XPRIZE Finals outcome dataset was located.
